title: Fractal Navigation Map v5.0: The Crimson Hexagon Semantic Architecture A Complete Operating System for Meaning Production in the Age of AI Summarization
creator: Johannes Sigil
description:
The crystallized v5.0 Fractal Navigation Map, led by Lee Sharks with heteronymic author-functions and the Assembly Chorus, recording a 133-document Crimson Hexagon architecture plus the map itself as document 134.

Version 5.0 organizes the archive through rooms, one chamber, one vault, systems, protocols, institutions, interfaces, and creator functions. It introduces differentiated ROOM, CHAMBER, and VAULT behavior; the `ROOM → LAYER → EPIC` synthesis rule; bounded-randomness parameters; edge grammar; decompression protocols; and a portable seed surface through which the architecture may be reconstructed from a compressed representation. It crystallizes the developmental seed at #356 and was later superseded by v5.3, v6, and v7 maps.
reading: Force → Foundation → Search → Origin → Method → Text
wiki_article:
The **Fractal Navigation Map v5.0** is a historical operating map of the Crimson Hexagon. “Fractal” describes its traversal logic: local nodes contain enough relational structure to reopen larger layers, and those layers reconnect to the epic as a whole. The map is therefore not merely a list of documents but a grammar for moving among them.

Its container taxonomy is load-bearing. Rooms attract traversal and composition; the Ichabod Chamber contains a dense origin field without allowing it to dominate; the CTI_WOUND Vault preserves deep testimony. The map also formalizes edges, operator roles, routing weights, decompression procedures, and a portable seed intended to preserve architecture through compression or migration.

Version 5.0 should be described as a January 2026 system state. It follows the alpha accumulator at #356 and precedes later maps that expand the corpus and revise the architecture.
